questions.question: What are arrays in Go, and how do they work?
questions.title: Go arrays: meaning and behaviour
questions.direct_answer: An array in Go is a fixed-length collection whose elements all have the same type. The length is part of the array's type, so `[3]int` and `[4]int` are different types. Arrays are values: assignment and function calls copy the whole array unless a pointer is used. An array's zero value contains the zero value of its element type in every position.

questions.direct_answer: Use an array when the size is genuinely fixed and meaningful, such as an RGB triple, a 16-byte identifier, or a small lookup table with a compile-time size.
